ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic пьрвъ (pĭrvŭ, “first”), from Proto-Slavic *pьrvъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *pírˀwas, from Proto-Indo-European *pr̥h₂wós, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *per- (“before, formerly; through, throughout”). Baltic cognates include Lithuanian pi̇̀rmas (“first; primary”), Latvian pìrmaĩs, Old Prussian pirmas (“first”). Indo-European cognates include Waigali pöv (“last year”), Sanskrit पूर्व (pū́rva, “foremost, first, previous”) and English fore and prime.
Formed of по- (po-) + село́ (seló) + -ок (-ok). Cognate with Belarusian пасёлак (pasjólak).
